[BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Witnessing the month here means being present at one's place of residence, whether a town or village.
[BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Al-shahr is accusative as a temporal adverb, not an object, because both residents and travelers witness the month.
[BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The phrase means let him fast in it: a preposition is omitted and the verb is extended directly to the governed noun.
[BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The resident who must fast is a rational, mature, healthy person; children and the insane may be present in town but are not obligated.
[BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | This binding command abrogates the resident's former choice between fasting, breaking the fast, and paying fidya.
[BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r7] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The illness concession applies even to a resident, and the travel concession even to a healthy person; ʿalā here means fī.
[BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r8] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | A sick person or traveler who breaks the fast must make up the missed days later.
[BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r9] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The earlier verse allowed residents able to fast, travelers, and the sick to choose; this verse removes the resident's choice, so the concession is restated to show it remains for the sick and traveler.
[BURSEVI:v1p239/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · نجم الدين | reports | Najm al-Dīn says to attend to the ease that accompanies hardship while obeying a command; like a patient taking bitter medicine for health, the wise focus on its benefit and drink with resolve.
[BURSEVI:v1p239/r10] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · النبي عليه السلام | reports | The Prophet reports seeing at the Lote Tree a vast, radiant angel assigned to glorify God on behalf of him and his community for Ramadan; two locked chests before the angel hold the community's deliverance from Hell, and no grading is stated.
[BURSEVI:v1p239/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · السعدي | reports | Saʿdī's couplet illustrates that a wise physician's bitter medicine is beneficial, like sugar given to a sick person.
[BURSEVI:v1p239/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Completing the prescribed total means making up the days missed because of illness or travel after Ramadan's fast was imposed.
[BURSEVI:v1p239/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The instruction to make up fasts on later days leaves their arrangement unrestricted, so they may be consecutive or separated; magnifying God means praising Him.
[BURSEVI:v1p239/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Mā is a verbal noun: the phrase means praising God for guiding you to a way of discharging the duty.
[BURSEVI:v1p239/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The fast-breaking concession is granted so that people thank God for this blessing with tongue, heart, and body.
[BURSEVI:v1p239/r7] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | reports | A hadith says whoever keeps three things is truly God's friend, and whoever neglects them is truly God's enemy: prayer, fasting, and the bath after major ritual impurity; no grading is given.
[BURSEVI:v1p239/r8] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | reports | A report says Paradise longs for four groups: Ramadan fasters, Qurʾan reciters, those who guard their tongues, and those who feed neighbors; no grading is given.
[BURSEVI:v1p239/r9] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | reports | A report says God forgives the Muslim at iftar for the sins of the limbs and thoughts his body and heart have engaged in; no grading is given.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | “The month of Ramadan” may be the subject, with the relative clause as predicate, introducing the obligation by the month’s merit.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r10] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | “Month” derives from a root meaning that something appeared, as months mark worship and transactions and become publicly known.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r11] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Al-Alusi accepts Ramadan as a verbal noun from “to burn”; he faults al-Bahr for denying verbal nouns from intransitive verbs.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r12] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalil derives Ramadan from “ramad,” a pre-autumn rain that cleans the earth of dust.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r13] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Al-Alusi says the compound month-name conventionally applies to Ramadan and the two Rabi months.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r14] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | A mnemonic says “month” is added only before names beginning with rāʾ, except Rajab, where that usage was not heard.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r15] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | The compound analysis derives rules for declension and the article from the second element.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r16] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | On that account, bare “Ramadan” in “whoever fasts Ramadan” drops one element of the compound to avoid ambiguity.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r17] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Acceptability of adding a generic noun to a specific one depends on usage and taste, not an absolute rule.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Alternatively, “whoever witnesses the month” is the predicate, with fā licensed by its conditional sense.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | It may predicate an omitted “that is the time when fasting was prescribed,” or identify the prescribed month.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | It may be whole-apposition to fasting, estimating “fasting the month of Ramadan”; the intervening words still relate to “was prescribed.”
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | rejects | An inclusion-apposition avoids estimating a genitive, but is less fitting because the previous fasting ruling is the main point and does not anticipate an apposition.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | A reading with “month” in the accusative construes it as the object of an omitted “fast.”
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · قيل | reports | Another accusative parse makes it object of “that you fast,” but this separates parts of the verbal noun construction.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · قيل | reports | It is also parsed as object of “you know,” estimating the month’s merit; a literal reading means knowing the month itself, which al-Alusi rejects.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | A month is a period beginning with sighting the new moon; “ashhur” is the plural for a few and “shuhur” for many.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · أكثر النحويين | reports | Most grammarians allow “month” to be added to every month-name, contrary to the claim that only three such forms are attested.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r10] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · أنس وعائشة | reports | A report attributed to the Prophet through Anas and Aisha also explains the name by sins burning in Ramadan.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r11] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Another explanation is that the month fell during burning heat when ancient month-names were transferred; its old name was Natiq.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r12] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن إسحاق | reports | Ibn Ishaq says revelation of the Qur’an began in Ramadan on the Night of Power.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r13] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن عباس وابن جبير والحسن | reports | Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and Hasan say the Qur’an descended all at once to the lowest heaven, then gradually to earth over twenty-three years.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · أدب الكاتب | reports | Adab al-Katib describes the limited forms as a scribal convention from Umar’s calendar, not a rule of language.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · سيبويه | reports | Sibawayh allows “month” with all month-names: including it is non-generic, while omitting it gives the generic sense.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · النحاة | reports | Grammarians report both declinable and indeclinable “Ibn Dayah”; a cited verse illustrates the form, with competing compound analyses.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | prefers | Al-Alusi concludes that Ramadan alone is a generic proper name for the known month.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · أبو هريرة | reports | A report from Abu Hurayra, both attributed to the Prophet and stopped at the Companion, forbids saying “Ramadan” because it is a divine name; say “month of Ramadan.”
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid adopts the prohibition on saying “Ramadan” alone.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | prefers | Al-Alusi’s correct view permits “Ramadan” alone, citing its use in sound hadith, while acknowledging caution.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن عمرو | reports | Ibn Amr explains the name by saying sins are burned away in that month.
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · قيل | reports | Another view understands the Qur’an’s descent in Ramadan as the revelation about Ramadan, namely the command to fast. | mentions 2:183
[ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r10] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | “Witnessed” can mean physical presence or knowledge of the month; both senses are proposed.

[BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p196/r4] BINTSHATI-IJAZ, d. 1419 · author | holds | The two verses address different cases, not abrogation: fidya applies to those described as yutīqūnahu, while the sick or traveler makes up missed days after the excuse ends.
[BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p196/r5] BINTSHATI-IJAZ, d. 1419 · author | holds | A person who breaks the fast for illness or travel must make up the missed days after the excuse passes; fidya is not accepted as a substitute for that make-up fast.

[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r11] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | rejects | The author rejects abrogation among these verses: people struggling to fast retain the fidya option, and the sick-and-traveler concessions are repeated to show they too remain in force.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r12] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Takbir means embracing God’s greatness in the heart and expressing it verbally; Allahu akbar means God is greatest and most exalted.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r13] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Takbir acknowledges God’s unity and uniqueness: anything less than the greatest has a defect or limitation and cannot be God.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r14] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Takbir at the start of prayer, bowing, prostration, and sacrifice declares that worship belongs to God alone.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r15] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Eid prayers and sermons include takbir for the same reason, and takbir is also said after obligatory prayers on the days of Tashriq. | mentions 2:203
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r2] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | The Qur’an’s revelation to Muhammad began in the Hira cave in Mecca on Ramadan 27, 610 CE, and was completed over about 23 years at intervals God deemed fitting.

[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r4] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | God chose as the fasting month the month in which He began revealing the final guide and means of guidance for all humanity.
